entries.answer: A parting is the occasion of separating, and the word carries more finality than leaving does, which is why it appears in phrases rather than in ordinary speech. The useful contrast is between a parting that is expected and one that is sudden, since English marks the difference in the surrounding words rather than in the word itself. A parting of ways is a mutual and usually amicable separation, and the phrase survives from a much older sense of dividing property.

patterns: what does see someone off mean
entries.answer: To send somebody off is to see them leave at the start of a journey, and it is a public act with a ritual attached, which is why it is nearly always plural. Somebody staying behind sees them off; somebody going does not send themselves off. The word also means dismissing somebody harshly, and that second sense is common enough that the two are worth keeping apart in writing.

patterns: what to say when leaving a party
entries.answer: An exit line is the last thing said as a conversation ends, and it does more work than its size suggests, because the other person will remember it rather than the middle. The convention across cultures is to end warmly, but English also allows a joke at the very end, which is the most common way to signal that nothing has gone badly. What is avoided is a remark that needs a reply, since that does not end anything.

patterns: wrap up meaning in a meal
entries.answer: To wrap up means to finish something, and the word came from physical objects being tied up in a bundle, so it carries a sense of tidying as well as finishing. In a meeting it means formally closing the discussion rather than running out of time, and the two are not the same. The verb also works for eating a meal quickly, where the sense is finishing it off, and that use is common enough to be worth knowing.

patterns: what does remain in touch mean
difference between stay in touch and keep in touch
entries.answer: To remain in touch is to keep contact, and the word is the formal register of what is otherwise a very casual idea, being keep in touch. Remain adds a sense of continuing rather than resuming, which matters after a long gap. What makes the phrase social rather than practical is that it implies something will be done, and it is one of the promises people most often make and least often keep.
